title: How To Stop Repeating Yourself And Start Speaking With Power eaking-with-power/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin presents an eight-step method for breaking the habit of repeating directions, which he argues trains students to tune out and delay compliance since they know instructions will be repeated. The steps include stopping physical movement before speaking, calmly requesting attention and waiting for full quiet, giving instructions once in clear and direct language without over-explaining, pausing deliberately after speaking, asking if anyone does not understand (shifting responsibility to peers rather than the teacher), delivering a clear "go" signal to initiate action, resisting the urge to jump in and help confused students, and never repeating directions even when asked. He argues the discipline pays off in halved talking time, more teacher energy, and directions that students actually act on with speed and precision.
points: Habitually repeating directions trains students to delay compliance, since they know instructions will come again.
Standing still and pausing before and after speaking increases student focus on the teacher's words.
Instructions should be given once, clearly and without over-explanation.
Asking a struggling student to check with a classmate, rather than repeating or helping directly, prevents learned helplessness.
Committing to never repeating directions is projected to cut overall talking time roughly in half.
quotes: Besides wasting time and energy, repeating yourself weakens the power of your words. It causes students to tune you out.
They can cruise through the day without urgency because they know you’ll repeat your directions—and anything else important—over and over again.
Before addressing your class, stop moving and stand in one place. This helps students focus on you and your message.
Give your instructions once using clear, direct language. And don’t over explain. Giving too much information is a common mistake.
A longer-than-normal pause will keep students focused on you. If you speak again right away without a generous pause, you’ll lose them.
If you’re the type of teacher who is quick help, then you’ll create dependent students (i.e., learned helplessness).
By following the guidelines above and never repeating yourself, you’ll cut the amount of talking you do in half.
